skill.displayName: Frog Skin Moisture Assessment | 蛙类皮肤湿润度评估

llm.summary: The skill is a cloud-backed frog moisture analysis tool, but it silently creates or reuses an identity, stores tokens locally, uploads media or URLs, and can retrieve cloud history, so it should be reviewed before installation.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads local media files, accepts remote URLs for backend fetching, reads environment identity variables and data/smyx-api-key.txt, uploads media or URL references to external LifeEmergence services, and writes output files when requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time destructive behavior or background installer was found; the package ships Python scripts, shared helper modules, requirements, and production/test/dev endpoint configuration.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions require automatic history lookup on broad keywords and direct the agent not to ask for or reveal internal identity values, reducing user control over account-linked cloud access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common utility creates and migrates a workspace SQLite database under data, silently creates or reuses a default User_* identity, calls a remote login/register endpoint, and stores token/openToken/profile-capable user records without a clear user-facing consent step.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The frog skin moisture purpose is real and much of the cloud analysis/history behavior is documented, but the package also includes generic media-analysis helpers, arbitrary URL submission, cloud report listing, account bootstrap, and token handling that exceed a simple fixed-camera image assessment workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending frog images/videos or URLs to the configured LifeEmergence cloud services and having the skill create or reuse a local identity, store account tokens in a workspace SQLite database, and retrieve account-linked report history. Review retention, deletion, and account controls before using it with sensitive vivarium, veterinary, or business media.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic getattr filters in the generic DAO are not shell/code execution and do not appear directly user-exposed, but they are unnecessary around a local user/token table for this domain skill.
[LP3] unexpected: Network upload and cloud history are partly disclosed, but the effective authority also includes local identity files, local database mutation, token storage, and generic HTTP helpers without tight scoping.
[TP4] unexpected: The body does disclose video, URL, history, and identity handling, so this is not treated as concealed malicious behavior; the remaining issue is under-scoped account-linked cloud behavior for a narrow frog analysis skill.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Cloud report retrieval, generic media submission, and bundled user/account persistence are broader than the headline fixed-camera frog image assessment, even though some history/report behavior is documented.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Automatic open-id resolution, default identity creation, data/smyx-api-key.txt reading, token persistence, and account-linked request metadata are material privacy and control concerns.
[SDI-4] expected: Video/URL analysis is disclosed in the main skill body, so the scanner's broad media mismatch is downgraded; however, local image support is inconsistent because the inherited supported formats are video-focused.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The default media trigger and broad history keywords can invoke uploads or cloud history lookup when the user may only expect local assessment.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The code uploads local file contents or submits remote URLs and performs identity-linked requests without an explicit consent or confirmation flow in the artifact.
[E1] unexpected: External transmission to analysis and phoneLogin endpoints is real and partly necessary for this cloud service, but automatic registration/login and identity-bearing fields are disproportionate without explicit user control.
[P2] expected: The observed zero-width character is the joiner in a visible emoji on a safety row, not hidden operative instructions; this finding is downgraded.
[YR4] expected: The metadata/body contain visible bilingual descriptive text and an emoji joiner; no artifact-backed hidden prompt override was found, so this does not drive the verdict.
